note: Feel numbers that are not physical (physical ones live in reality.json). Camera rows sized against hero.height 1.89 m.

camera.note_fade: fade_near and fade_far: m from the lens to the hero's drawn box, gone from fade_near in, solid from fade_far out, the whole body as one in between (it was a per-pixel dither by each fragment's distance, which showed as a dot pattern over the pack and helmet in a tight room). lift_full: m of free arm behind the pivot at which a wall behind lifts the view all the way to pitch_min
camera.note_follow: follow_rate: 1/s, the pivot's critically damped spring (it trails a steady walk by 2 v / rate); follow_limit: m it may trail; rise_rate: 1/s, the pivot's height toward the floor, slower than across; lead_time: s of velocity the aim looks ahead in a steady run; lead_rate: 1/s, how slowly that lead builds and goes; recentre_after: s of no look input before the yaw drifts behind the real travel; recentre_per_m: rad of drift per rad of error per metre travelled (a leash, so it never turns while the hero stands or pushes a wall)
camera.note_rush: a vehicle's speed framing (follow_cam.gd), reached at its top speed and eased by lead_rate: rush_distance and rush_height are shares of the vehicle distance and pivot height (9 m and 2.4 m become 7.2 m and 1.9 m), rush_lead s of velocity the aim looks ahead (lead_time on foot). The field of view never changes (skills/third-person-camera rule 14). Our choice, 13 Nov playtest: "I felt the rover is slow"
camera.note_frame: frame_low: share of the frame height the pivot sits below centre when looking level (1/6 is the lower-third line), easing to centred at pitch_min; slope_ahead: m ahead along the view where a ray reads the ground; slope_share: share of that slope the view pitches by; slope_max_deg: the most it pitches. follow_rate and lead_rate also set the lead that cancels the spring's lag in a steady walk (2 v / follow_rate, built at lead_rate)

hop.note: xfade: s of blend between clips; anticipation: s of crouch before take-off, the last part of hop_start plays in it (all 0.34 s of it would delay every press); xfade_hop: s of blend into and out of the hop clips, short so the arc keeps its timing

hero.note: gait_hysteresis: Froude the hurry-to-walk change sits below hero.froude.walk_run. The boots' sink is reality.json hero.sink; smooth_deg: at load the hero's normals are averaged across edges flatter than this angle, so the suit's folds shade smooth and the pack's box corners (90 deg) stay sharp; the limbs are about eight-sided, 45 deg a face, which 40 left faceted (the file's normals were split face by face)

coat.note: Where the suit gathers the design's dust coat (DESIGN.md weathering: its colour, its amount by sky state, each role's share; the visor's share is 0), by analogy with Apollo: dust 'quickly and effectively coated' boots, gloves and suits, and wore through 'above boot' (Gaier 2005); no Mars EVA has happened. legs_top: m above the soles where the kicked-up dust has faded out (the knee is about 0.5 m up); knees: the front of the thighs, knees and shins (kneeling, falls); hands, forearms: gloves and forearms (tools and samples); torso: helmet shell, chest and back, light; pack_top: the top of the backpack, by how level it is; patch: m across a patch of thicker or thinner dust; max: the most of the coat any part shows; chroma: the share of the dust's hue the suit takes (the rest is its brightness, a grey-brown stain): with the dust's full hue the storm turned the suit orange, and an orange astronaut vanishes against Mars (project rule). Both keep the hero a dusty white with readable teal bands. All art direction, judged in day and storm captures.

audio.note: The mix (audio/audio.gd). dB on top of the files, which are normalised (loops -20 LUFS, one-shots -3 dBFS peak). range: m, a 3D sound's cut-off, Mars sound 'falters at just 26 feet (8 meters)' (NASA/JPL 2022); unit_size: m where a 3D sound starts to fall away. fade_s: s of the inside/outside crossfade. breath: rest in breaths a minute, a resting adult takes 12 to 18 (MedlinePlus, Vital signs); hard (at the sheet's hurry speed), rise_s and fall_s (time constants: up fast, settling back slowly) and inhale_share (where in a breath the exhale starts) are art direction, never shown to players. wind: ref_speed m/s that plays at wind.db (sky states blow 4 to 6, world.json weather); gust: the swell's share; gust_hz: its slow noise frequency. habitat and machines: world.json item ids. pitch: random spread on one-shots. music: db of a cue (files at about -16 LUFS), fade_s its fade in, gap_s the least silence between two cues (rare by design: skills/living-atmosphere), art direction, never shown to players

rover.note: sandbox/rover.gd, art direction (the physical rows are reality.json rover.*). travel: m each wheel's suspension takes up either way before the body tilts; wheel_shade and body_shade: [radius m, strength 0 to 1] of the moving contact shadow under each wheel pair and under the body's two halves (world.touch(), shaded like data/world.json grounding)

life.note: The hero's layers on top of its clips (player/hero_life.gd), art direction judged on film; the limits that are physical come from the sheet (hero.lean.max). lean_share: share of the free-body angle atan(a / g) the upper body leans into a push; lean_hz and lean_damping: its spring (under 1 swings a little past upright at a stop); carry_lean_deg: extra forward lean over a carried bag; breath_chest_deg and breath_shoulder_deg: how far the chest tips back and the shoulders rise at a full breath (the clock and rate are audio.breath's); look_waist_deg, look_head_deg, look_pitch_deg: each side, the waist takes most of a turn because a helmet turns with the torso (no sheet row: suited neck and waist ranges were not found); look_rate: 1/s the gaze's angles ease toward a new aim (angles, not the point: a point eased across the body flips the turn); look_far: m ahead along the camera's view the gaze rests when nothing is near; the waist's share fades out with the pace (a walker looks with the head). carry_swing_deg: each arm swings out about the vertical at the shoulder while a bag is held, so the gloves and forearms meet its sides instead of going into it; carry_out: m the bag rides ahead of the clip's hold point, so the chest does not go into its back (the clip was posed for a thinner bag); both found with tests/player_test.gd carry_hands (the drawn hero at most 1 cm inside the cargo bag over a walk cycle); carry_swing_s: s to swing in or out, the clip's crossfade
